thin.$description: Decorative/non-interactive strokes — hairlines, static card borders, dividers (app-design spec §1.4: simplified to a flat 1px, dropping the 0.8px diagram-tool value that existed only for sub-pixel leaf-node outlines).

default.$description: Most strokes — same 1px decorative value as `thin` (app-design spec §1.4 collapses the old three-step 0.8/1/1.2px ramp to a plain decorative/interactive pair).

strong.$description: Interactive strokes — focus rings, hover/focus/error borders, checked/selected states (app-design spec §1.4: 2px, up from 1.2px — the old value only had to survive the website's now-removed cut-corner notch shape at fractional-pixel rendering).

sm.$description: Square corners everywhere (app-design spec §1.4) — no rounding, kept as a token (not deleted) so a future true circle still has `full` to reach for and every consumer keeps calling `.borderRadiusAll(radiusSm())` unchanged.

full.$description: The one deliberate exception to `radius.*: 0` — true circles only (avatars, status dots), app-design spec §1.4.

unit.$description: Every coord, size, and gap divisible by this — hard rule, matches diagram-design's own grid constraint

1.$description: 1x grid.unit. Icon padding, tight inline gaps.

3.$description: 3x grid.unit. Comfortable inline gap, form field padding.

4.$description: 4x grid.unit. Default block gap, card padding.

24.$description: 24x grid.unit. Landing-section block padding, incl. the hero's — matches the reference site's `--space-9`. A hero that sits under a `position: fixed` nav (which overlays page content) needs a much larger top padding (192px) to clear it; this template's nav is `position: sticky` (in-flow, not overlaying), so the hero needs only the ordinary section padding, not an extra nav-clearing allowance.
